---
title: "Data Preparation for Edge Bundling"
format: html
---

## Setup

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(here)
```

## Parse Upstream Data Sources for Network Analysis

To construct our hierarchical edge bundling plot, we extract the lineage of each dataset. Datasets can be derived directly from remote sensing (`inputRemote`) or statistical data (`inputStat`), or indirectly via existing land cover maps (`inputMap`).

```{r parse-edges}
# Load dataset from Excel workbook
df_sorted <- read_excel(here("agri_data_review.xlsx"), sheet = "Sorted") |>
    mutate(nameShort = str_squish(nameShort)) |>
    filter(!is.na(nameShort), nameShort != "")

# 1. Parse all direct dependencies into a flat list
all_deps <- df_sorted |>
    select(target = nameShort, inputMap, inputRemote, inputStat) |>
    pivot_longer(
        cols = c(inputMap, inputRemote, inputStat),
        names_to = "input_field",
        values_to = "source"
    ) |>
    mutate(
        input_type = case_when(
            input_field == "inputRemote" ~ "Remotely Sensed",
            input_field == "inputStat" ~ "In Situ & Survey Data",
            input_field == "inputMap" ~ "Map",
            TRUE ~ NA_character_
        )
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(input_type), !is.na(source), source != "") |>
    separate_rows(source, sep = "[,;]") |>
    mutate(source = str_squish(source)) |>
    filter(source != "", source != "?") |>
    distinct(target, input_type, source)

# 2. Restrict target datasets to agriculture and group them by category
agri_targets <- df_sorted |>
    filter(str_to_lower(str_squish(focus)) == "agriculture") |>
    mutate(dataset_group = if_else(is.na(category) | str_squish(category) == "", "Crops", category)) |>
    mutate(dataset_group = factor(dataset_group, levels = c(
        "Combined Agroecosystem", "Crops", "Grassland", "Livestock",
        "Intensity & Management", "Fertilizer", "Pesticide"
    ))) |>
    select(dataset = nameShort, dataset_group)

# 3. Resolve Transitive Dependencies
# Direct links (Remotely Sensed and In Situ & Survey Data)
direct_rs <- all_deps |>
    filter(target %in% agri_targets$dataset, input_type %in% c("Remotely Sensed", "In Situ & Survey Data")) |>
    rename(dataset = target)

# Indirect dependencies via inputMaps
direct_maps <- all_deps |>
    filter(target %in% agri_targets$dataset, input_type == "Map") |>
    rename(dataset = target)

map_sources <- all_deps |>
    filter(target %in% direct_maps$source, input_type %in% c("Remotely Sensed", "In Situ & Survey Data"))

# Link map usage back to base sources
transitive_rs <- direct_maps |>
    inner_join(map_sources, by = c("source" = "target"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    select(dataset, input_type = input_type.y, source = source.y)

# Combine, unique, and join with dataset groups
links <- bind_rows(direct_rs, transitive_rs) |>
    distinct() |>
    inner_join(agri_targets, by = "dataset", relationship = "many-to-many")

if (nrow(links) == 0) {
    stop("No lineage links found after filtering. Check data.")
}

# 4. Save processed links for downstream visualization
dir.create(here("data", "processed"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write_csv(links, here("data", "processed", "network_links.csv"))

head(links)
```
